recommendation:
BOTTOM LINE. Use laurenceyoon/live-lyrics-tracking as a design reference and a small evaluation corpus. Don't use it as a code base. The repo is PRIVATE and has no LICENSE (the GitHub API returns license=null and /license gives 404), so its code and checkpoints are all-rights-reserved. The CRNN checkpoints were trained only on TIMIT, which is an LDC-licensed corpus. The algorithm itself is published openly: Park, Yong, Kwon, Nam, "A Real-Time Lyrics Alignment System Using Chroma and Phonetic Features for Classical Vocal Performance", ICASSP 2024, arXiv:2401.09200, CC BY 4.0. Reimplement from that paper and from Dixon 2005 OLTW. The owner, laurenceyoon, is Jiyun Park (KAIST MACLab; commit author "jiyun.park"; the paper links github.com/laurenceyoon/winterreise_rt). The user can read the private repo, so they probably have collaborator access. Get written permission from her before copying any code or .pt files, and never put them in a public repo.

WHAT THE SYSTEM ACTUALLY IS. It works in two phases and uses reference audio as a stand-in for the score.

(1) Offline phase:
- MusicXML → per-note lyric syllables (music21), timed at a forced 120 bpm.
- A MuseScore/MIDI render (*_score.wav) is aligned to a real recording (*_ref.wav) with synctoolbox MrMsDTW, using chroma_cens + DLNCO at 16 kHz and 25 fps.
- The result is stored as a warping-path CSV.

(2) Online phase, audio-to-audio OLTW between the ref and the live mic:
- 16 kHz, hop 640 (40 ms, 25 fps), 160 ms chunks (4 frames).
- Features: 12-d chroma_stft (n_fft 1280, center=False, L∞-normalised) stacked with a 5-class phonetic posteriorgram (PPG) from a causal CRNN (softmax then log1p(5p)/4, max 0.448), so 17 dimensions.
- Cosine distance; window of 5 s in the app (3 s in the paper); MAX_RUN_COUNT 30 in the app (3 in the evaluation).
- Display look-ahead ADJUST_DELAY = 5 frames (200 ms).
- The position goes to Redis, and a FastAPI WebSocket polls it every 10 ms and pushes JSON to a React page.

The thesis-era code (commit 8725d8d) converted the ref position to score beats through the warping path. HEAD instead compares the ref position directly with DB timestamps that came from LRC files tapped on the ref audio. So the 2023 pieces (Heidenröslein, 꽃밭에서, Ave Maria), whose DB times are in score time, are not handled correctly by HEAD.

How this maps onto our design:
- Our offline phase becomes: vocal separation + syllabification + forced alignment on the ref, giving syllable timings in ref time. No MusicXML is needed.
- Mode (a): ref features come from the full mix.
- Mode (b): ref features come from the separated vocal stem.
- Keep the 25 fps grid and the chroma+PPG idea.
- Compute ref features through exactly the same streaming code path as the live input (chunked, stateful LSTM, same dB clamping) to avoid train/test mismatch.

OLTW PROBLEMS TO FIX IN A CLEAN-ROOM REIMPLEMENTATION (all verified by reading backend/app/core/online_dtw.py at HEAD f8396bb):

(a) init_matrix:
- Slices target_features[:, min(y-d,0):y]; it should be max(y-d,0). This is harmless only because init runs once at y=d.
- The path-length matrix starts at len=0 at (0,0), so it is off by one.
- In the j==0 branch it adds local_dist to the length matrix instead of +1.

(b) select_candidate:
- Uses `min_idx <= len(norm_x_edge)`; it should be `<`. When the minimum is the first cell of the live edge, it is misread as the corner and triggers a REF step.
- Candidate coordinates mix an exclusive end (wx or wy) with 0-based indices. This adds a systematic +1-frame (40 ms) bias on the edge axis.

(c) There is no BOTH step: a corner minimum always advances only the ref.

(d) The diagonal predecessor is multiplied by 0.98 on the accumulated cost instead of using additive step weights:
- This works like exponential forgetting (about 50 diagonal steps, roughly 2 s) on diagonal moves only, which makes acc/len normalisation inconsistent.
- In my simulation, diagonal choices went from 48% to 58% of cells as the absolute cost level grew.
- Use Dixon/Müller additive weights (1,1,2)·d and normalise by i+j instead.

(e) The app publishes ref_pointer (the window frontier), not the best-matching ref frame. Separately, match_eval evaluates candi_history (the internal path), so the evaluated signal is not what the screen shows.

(f) Warm-up: ref_pointer is preset to w=125 frames and QUERY is forced until 125 live frames arrive. So for the first 5 s the display is pinned to ref time ≈5.2 s, which is wrong for songs that start singing immediately (Lascia starts at 0.30 s, 꽃밭에서 at about 2.5 s in the ref). There is also no start detection or re-localisation: once lost by more than the window, it never recovers.

(g) Streaming-path issues:
- The PortAudio callback runs the feature computation and the CRNN inline, which risks input overflow.
- feature_buffer is unbounded, so latency grows silently if the tracker falls behind.
- The live CRNN resets its LSTM state every 160 ms chunk and gets only 640 samples + 2 mel frames of context, while the ref is processed with full context.
- AmplitudeToDB(top_db=80) clamps per call, so the live input is clamped relative to the chunk maximum and the ref relative to the song maximum.
- The evaluation notebook hides these by using additional_buffer = CHUNK_SIZE*64 (10.24 s of audio re-processed every chunk).

(h) Housekeeping:
- run() calls librosa.get_duration(filename=...) on every iteration; the `filename` keyword was removed in librosa 1.0.0 (2026-08-11).
- WebsocketManager.broadcast deletes stale connections by ascending index (wrong connections get deleted).
- Every connected client runs its own 100 Hz loop that broadcasts to all clients, so traffic grows as N².

A tested clean sketch is at scratchpad/research/reference-repo/scripts/oltw_clean.py. On a synthetic tempo-varying sequence (0.8–1.25×) it gives mean 68 ms, median 38 ms, 92% within 200 ms. The reference-style Python strip update costs about 0.58 ms for w=125, d=4 on this M5 Pro (Python 3.14), so OLTW compute is not the bottleneck; CRNN/PPG inference and feature extraction are.

FEATURES AND MODEL:
- uni-5cls-640hop.pt is a CRNN: ConvStack 64-64-128 channels → FC 2048→1024 → unidirectional LSTM 1024 → Linear 5. About 10.6M parameters, 46.8 MB.
- Its input is a 66-bin nnAudio mel spectrogram (n_fft = win_length = 1024 per the checkpoint config, although the paper says 1280; hop 640; fmin 0, fmax 8000; dB with top_db 80) computed from 16 kHz mono float audio.
- It was trained with framewise cross-entropy on TIMIT (English read speech) only. Every shipped checkpoint (5cls-640, 5cls-320, 14cls, 39cls, 61cls) has dataset = TIMIT.
- Classes (from timit5.phoneset, with index 0 = vowels confirmed by the repo's vowel-rate code): 0 vowels/glides/liquids, 1 stops/affricates, 2 fricatives + hh, 3 nasals, 4 silence/closures.
- The five broad classes are close to language-universal, and the PPG is only compared audio-to-audio (ref and live both pass through the same model). That is why the authors used it for Korean at IK2023, but there is no Korean or Japanese evaluation.
- Expect degradation on full mixes (mode a) and on singing in general.
- Chroma is not transposition-invariant. winterreise_rt pitch-shifted the target to the ref key before evaluating, so a real system needs key-offset handling (an optimal-transposition-index estimate at start, or the minimum over circular chroma shifts).

EVALUATION HARNESS. Build three tiers.

Tier 1 — SWD / winterreise_rt (real human note ground truth, German):
- Rebuild from SWD v2.1 (Zenodo record 10839767, CC BY 3.0, 517 MB zip). Audio exists only for HU33 and SC06; there are 24 songs with voice-note annotations (semicolon-delimited CSV; keep instrument == voice).
- Use ref = HU33 and live = SC06. Run once transposed to the ref key, as the paper did, for comparability, and once untransposed as a stress test.
- Derive syllable ground truth from score lyrics mapped to notes by index.
- Baseline to beat (paper, Table 1):
  - Online chroma+Phoneme5: AAE 376 ms, MedAE 136 ms, PCO 64.75 / 75.49 / 85.82 / 92.26 % at 200 / 300 / 500 / 1000 ms.
  - Offline score→ref chroma+DLNCO: AAE 302 ms, MedAE 137 ms, PCO 67.7 / 83.4 / 93.3 / 98.1 %.
  - Chroma only: AAE 1366 ms.

Tier 2 — the repo's own resources (details in key_facts):
- Edelweiss.wav + LRC: English, offline ground truth.
- Edelweiss.wav ↔ Edelweiss_short.wav: the only real two-performance pair, English, 26 identical tokens.
- Lascia ch'io pianga: Italian, offline ground truth.
- 꽃밭에서: Korean, 144-syllable pseudo ground truth from the warping path.
- Heidenröslein (German) and Ave Maria (Latin): pseudo ground truth.
- There is no Japanese ground truth at all; it must be created.

Tier 3 — synthetic warps:
- Time-varying time-stretch, plus pitch shift, noise, reverb and EQ, applied to any ref (mix or stem). The ground truth is exact, so this scales to Korean and Japanese.

Metrics:
- The paper's AAE, MedAE and PCO@τ.
- Prompter metrics computed on the published (displayed) position, not the internal path: sample-and-hold ref-position error at ground-truth live onsets (signed bias plus AAE), highlight latency (first live time the displayed position reaches the ground-truth ref onset), lost fraction (error > 2 s), recovery time, and real-time factor / CPU.
- Measure latency with real-time-paced mock streaming. The reference's mock stream feeds audio as fast as possible, which hides latency.
- Builders and metrics are tested in scratchpad/research/reference-repo/scripts/gt_and_metrics.py.

ENVIRONMENT IMPLICATIONS:
- synctoolbox 1.4.2 (2026-05-20) requires librosa>=0.11,<1.0, numba>=0.63,<0.66, numpy>=2.0,<2.5 and Python >=3.10,<3.15. If synctoolbox is used for ground-truth generation, pin librosa 0.11.x rather than 1.0.0.
- Run synctoolbox pitch/DLNCO features at 22050 Hz. Its filterbank is hard-coded for 22050/4410/882 Hz, and the reference fed it 16 kHz.
- Replace PyAudio callbacks with sounddevice 0.5.6, using a callback that only enqueues audio.
- Replace attributedict with a dataclass.

alternatives.name: Fork / copy the reference code and CRNN checkpoints as-is
alternatives.pros: Fastest demo. Already used live at Innovate Korea 2023/2024 events. Full stack (FastAPI + Redis + SQLite + React) and five TIMIT PPG checkpoints already exist.
alternatives.cons: Private repo with no LICENSE (all rights reserved), and the checkpoints come from LDC-licensed TIMIT. Several DP bugs: init length matrix, '<=' edge bug, inconsistent candidate coordinates, multiplicative 0.98 diagonal, frontier reported instead of best match, 5 s start-up pin. Breaks on librosa 1.0 (get_duration filename=). Heavy compute inside the PortAudio callback. Live/ref CRNN mismatch (LSTM state reset per chunk, per-chunk dB clamping). Polling architecture: 100 Hz per client, N² broadcast. The requirements pin the wrong 'whisper' package (Graphite DB).

alternatives.name: Clean-room Dixon OLTW reimplementation with our own features (RECOMMENDED)
alternatives.pros: License-clean: based on Dixon 2005 and the CC BY 4.0 paper. Fixes all the identified bugs (additive (1,1,2) weights, i+j normalisation, BOTH step, best-match position output, start-up handling, run limit 3). Can add re-localisation, key-offset handling and a stateful streaming feature path shared by ref and live. Easy to unit-test against synthetic warps. A tested sketch exists (oltw_clean.py: 68 ms mean error on a synthetic 0.8–1.25× warp).
alternatives.cons: More engineering. Needs our own PPG/acoustic model, either retrained on licensed or multilingual singing data or replaced with another phonetic feature. Must re-establish the SWD baseline ourselves to show parity with the paper (AAE 376 ms).

alternatives.name: pymatchmaker 0.3.0 (github.com/pymatchmaker/matchmaker) as the online aligner
alternatives.pros: Apache-2.0, actively maintained (pushed 2026-10-10, 91 stars). Real-time music alignment library with multiple followers (OLTW-style and HMM-style). Avoids writing the DP ourselves.
alternatives.cons: requires_python >=3.10,<3.13 (forces a 3.11/3.12 venv). Designed around piano/score following. I have not verified that it accepts arbitrary precomputed feature matrices (chroma+PPG) or that its latency and API fit a WebSocket prompter. Adds a dependency surface.

alternatives.name: Keep the reference's MusicXML → score-audio → synctoolbox offline path
alternatives.pros: Produces dense note/syllable pseudo ground truth on real recordings whenever a MusicXML exists. Useful for building evaluation data (that is how 꽃밭에서/Heidenröslein/Ave Maria were labelled). Paper-reported offline accuracy is AAE 302 ms, MedAE 137 ms.
alternatives.cons: The user's requirement is lyrics text + audio only, with no score. The ground-truth quality is itself algorithmic: about 33% of notes are off by more than 200 ms in the paper's own offline numbers. The reference ran the DLNCO filterbank at 16 kHz (it is designed for 22050). Fragile tempo handling: the Ave Maria score.wav is not at the 120 bpm used in the CSV.

key_facts.claim: The repo is private, created 2023-02-16, last push 2026-06-02 (commit f8396bb), has no LICENSE (API license=null, /license returns 404), 2 forks, 0 stars. Commit authors are jiyun.park, MACLab and seingreen.
The algorithm is published as Park, Yong, Kwon, Nam, ICASSP 2024 (arXiv:2401.09200, CC BY 4.0). It links github.com/laurenceyoon/winterreise_rt, so laurenceyoon = Jiyun Park, KAIST GSCT.

Paper Table 1 (winterreise_rt, 24 songs, voice-note level). Online Chroma+Phoneme5: AAE 376 ms, MedAE 136 ms, Std 630 ms, PCO 64.75 / 75.49 / 85.82 / 92.26 % at 200 / 300 / 500 / 1000 ms. Chroma only: AAE 1366 ms. Mel: AAE 1222 ms. Offline score→ref chroma+DLNCO: AAE 302 ms, MedAE 137 ms, PCO 67.71 / 83.35 / 93.31 / 98.1 %.

HEAD configuration: SAMPLE_RATE 16000, HOP 640 (25 fps), N_FFT 1280, CHUNK 2560 (160 ms), DTW_WINDOW_SIZE 5 s (125 frames; 3 s in the paper and the thesis code), MAX_RUN_COUNT 30 (3 in the evaluation notebooks), DISTANCE cosine, FEATURES ['chroma','phoneme'], N_MELS 66, ADJUST_DELAY 5 frames, DEVICE 'mps', TOLERANCES [200, 300, 500, 750, 1000] ms.

CRNN checkpoint uni-5cls-640hop.pt (46.8 MB) config: dataset train/valid/test = TIMIT, num_lbl 5, feature melspec, sr 16000, win_length 1024, hop 640, n_mels 66, fmin 0, fmax 8000, model_complexity 64, batch 16, num_frames 168, lr 1.83e-5 decaying 0.98 every 853 iterations, early stopping on f1_micro. Tensors: conv 64/64/128, fc (1024×2048), LSTM W_ih (4096×1024), unidirectional, out (5×1024), so about 10.6M parameters. The 14cls, 39cls, 61cls and 5cls-320hop checkpoints are also TIMIT-only.
key_facts.source: Inspected data.pkl with a restricted unpickler (scratchpad/research/reference-repo/scripts/inspect_ckpt.py)

key_facts.claim: PPG post-processing: logits (T+2 frames, with 2 cached mel frames prepended) → drop the first and last frame → softmax over classes → log1p(5p)/4. Stacked under 12-d chroma (norm=inf) to give 17-d frames; the paper found this weighting best.

5-class phone set (timit5.phoneset): aa = vowels+glides+liquids (aa,ae,ah,ao,aw,ax,axh,axr,ay,eh,el,er,ey,ih,ix,iy,l,ow,oy,r,uh,uw,ux,w,y); p = stops/affricates (p,t,k,b,d,g,jh,ch); s = fricatives + hh/hv; m = nasals; sil = closures/pauses/q/dx. Index 0 = vowels (the repo counts argmax==0 as the vowel rate).

OLTW bugs: init_matrix uses min(y-d,0) instead of max (harmless, called once at y=d); length matrix (0,0)=0, and the j==0 branch adds local_dist instead of 1; select_candidate uses '<=' instead of '<'; candidate mixes an exclusive end (wx/wy) with 0-based indices (+1 frame bias); no BOTH step; the diagonal uses acc*0.98 (multiplicative) instead of an additive weight; the app publishes ref_pointer (frontier) while the evaluation uses candi_history; ref_pointer is pinned at w (5 s) until the first 125 live frames arrive.
key_facts.source: backend/app/core/online_dtw.py (HEAD; identical DP code at thesis commit 8725d8d)

key_facts.claim: The 0.98 multiplicative diagonal raises diagonal choices from 48.4% to 57.9% of cells as the accumulated-cost offset grows from 0 to 1000, in a random-cost simulation.
key_facts.source: Local simulation (python3, numpy) in this session

key_facts.claim: Reference-style Python strip update (w=125, d=4) costs about 0.58 ms on the M5 Pro (Python 3.14, numpy 2.5.2); a leaner Python loop with additive weights costs about 0.23 ms. OLTW DP is not the real-time bottleneck.

Streaming mismatches: the live CRNN gets 640 samples of overlap plus 2 cached mel frames and a zero LSTM state every 160 ms chunk, while the ref is processed whole. AmplitudeToDB(top_db=80) clamps per call. The evaluation used additional_buffer = CHUNK_SIZE*64 (10.24 s of audio re-processed per chunk) to compensate. Feature extraction runs inside the PyAudio callback.

# Full tested files (clean-room, safe to adapt):
#   /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sunjaewon-projects-Performance-live-lyrics-tracking/a1551f14-1847-4d65-a2d8-137d02c33533/scratchpad/research/reference-repo/scripts/oltw_clean.py
#   /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sunjaewon-projects-Performance-live-lyrics-tracking/a1551f14-1847-4d65-a2d8-137d02c33533/scratchpad/research/reference-repo/scripts/gt_and_metrics.py
# Downloaded reference sources (read-only, do not redistribute): .../scratchpad/research/reference-repo/src/

# ---------- 1) Clean Dixon-style OLTW (fixes: additive (1,1,2) weights, i+j normalisation, BOTH step,
#               consistent absolute coords, best-match output instead of frontier) ----------
import numpy as np
class OLTW:
    REF, LIVE, BOTH = 0, 1, 2
    def __init__(self, X, c=75, max_run=3, w=(1.0, 1.0, 2.0)):   # X: (N,F) ref features @25 fps
        X = np.asarray(X, np.float64)
        self.X = X / (np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-9)   # cosine = 1 - dot
        self.N, self.c, self.max_run, self.w = len(X), c, max_run, w
        self.Y, self.cols = {}, {}            # live j -> unit vec ; live j -> [lo, [D(lo..)]]
        self.ni = self.nj = 0; self.prev, self.run, self.pos = None, 0, 0
    def _D(self, i, j):
        col = self.cols.get(j)
        if col is None or i < 0: return np.inf
        k = i - col[0]; return col[1][k] if 0 <= k < len(col[1]) else np.inf
    def _cell(self, i, j):
        d = 1.0 - float(self.X[i] @ self.Y[j])
        if i == 0 and j == 0: return d
        return min(self._D(i-1, j) + self.w[0]*d, self._D(i, j-1) + self.w[1]*d, self._D(i-1, j-1) + self.w[2]*d)
    def _add_live_col(self):
        j, lo = self.nj, max(0, self.ni - self.c)
        self.cols[j] = [lo, [self._cell(i, j) for i in range(lo, self.ni)]] if False else [lo, []]
        for i in range(lo, self.ni): self.cols[j][1].append(self._cell(i, j))
        self.nj += 1; self.cols.pop(j - self.c - 1, None); self.Y.pop(j - self.c - 1, None)
    def _add_ref_row(self):
        i = self.ni
        if i >= self.N: return
        for j in range(max(0, self.nj - self.c), self.nj):
            col = self.cols[j]
            if col[0] + len(col[1]) != i:
                if not col[1]: col[0] = i
                else: continue
            col[1].append(self._cell(i, j))
        self.ni += 1
    def _best(self):
        best, arg = np.inf, (self.ni-1, self.nj-1); jl = self.nj-1; lo, D = self.cols[jl]
        for k, v in enumerate(D):
            s = v / (lo + k + jl + 1)
            if s < best: best, arg = s, (lo + k, jl)
        il = self.ni-1
        for j in range(max(0, self.nj - self.c), self.nj):
            s = self._D(il, j) / (il + j + 1)
            if s < best: best, arg = s, (il, j)
        return arg
    def step(self, y):                         # feed ONE live frame; returns ref frame estimate
        y = np.asarray(y, np.float64); self.Y[self.nj] = y / (np.linalg.norm(y) + 1e-9)
        if self.nj == 0 and self.ni == 0: self._add_ref_row()
        self._add_live_col()
        while True:
            if self.nj < self.c: step = self.BOTH                       # warm-up lock-step
            else:
                bi, bj = self._best()
                if self.run >= self.max_run and self.prev in (self.REF, self.LIVE):
                    step = self.LIVE if self.prev == self.REF else self.REF
                elif bi < self.ni - 1: step = self.LIVE                 # ref ahead -> wait for input
                elif bj < self.nj - 1: step = self.REF                  # live ahead -> add ref rows
                else: step = self.BOTH
            self.run = self.run + 1 if step == self.prev else 1; self.prev = step
            if step in (self.REF, self.BOTH) and self.ni < self.N: self._add_ref_row()
            if step in (self.LIVE, self.BOTH) or self.ni >= self.N: break
        jl = self.nj - 1; lo, D = self.cols[jl]
        if D: self.pos = lo + int(np.argmin([v / (lo + k + jl + 1) for k, v in enumerate(D)]))
        return self.pos
# synthetic check (0.8-1.25x tempo warp + noise): mean 68 ms, median 38 ms, 92.4% < 200 ms

# ---------- 2) Ground truth from the reference resources ----------
import csv, re, unicodedata
from pathlib import Path
FPS = 25.0
def parse_lrc(path):  # repo flavour: '[mm:ss.xx]E  <mm:ss.xx>del  <mm:ss.xx>weiss,  <mm:ss.xx> e ...'
    out = []
    for li, raw in enumerate(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()):
        m = re.match(r"\[(\d+):(\d+\.\d+)\](.*)", raw)
        if not m: continue
        mi, se, rest = m.groups(); rest = rest.strip()
        if not rest.startswith("<"): rest = f"<{mi}:{se}> " + rest
        for a, b, txt in re.findall(r"<(\d+):(\d+\.\d+)>([^<]*)", rest):
            out.append(dict(t=int(a)*60+float(b), text=txt.strip(), word_start=txt.startswith(" "), line=li))
    return out
def strict_monotonic(wp):
    keep = np.r_[True, (np.diff(wp[:, 0]) > 0) & (np.diff(wp[:, 1]) > 0)]; keep[-1] = True; return wp[keep]
def score_csv_to_ref_gt(score_csv, wp_csv, sec_per_quarter=0.5):   # 1.5 for Ave_maria
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(score_csv, encoding="utf-8")))
    wp = strict_monotonic(np.loadtxt(wp_csv, delimiter=",")) / FPS     # cols: score_s, ref_s
    syl = [(float(r["offset"]) * sec_per_quarter, unicodedata.normalize("NFC", r["lyric"])) for r in rows if r["lyric"]]
    t_ref = np.interp([s[0] for s in syl], wp[:, 0], wp[:, 1])
    return [dict(text=s[1], t_score=s[0], t_ref=float(t)) for s, t in zip(syl, t_ref)]
# e.g. score_csv_to_ref_gt('resources/annots/꽃밭에서_score.csv','resources/alignments/꽃밭에서_offline.csv')
#  -> 144 syllables: 꽃 2.54 s, 밭 3.28 s, 에 4.31 s, 앉 4.56 s ... (pseudo-GT; spot-check by ear)
# Online EN pair: ref=Edelweiss.wav (parse_lrc(...)[:26]) vs live=Edelweiss_short.wav (parse_lrc(...)) - identical 26 tokens.

# ---------- 3) Metrics: paper metrics + display-based prompter metrics ----------
def alignment_errors(est, gt, tol_ms=(50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 1000)):
    e = np.abs(np.asarray(est) - np.asarray(gt))
    return dict(AAE_ms=1e3*e.mean(), MedAE_ms=1e3*np.median(e), Std_ms=1e3*e.std(),
                **{f"PCO@{t}": 100*np.mean(e <= t/1e3) for t in tol_ms})
def prompter_metrics(t_live, pos_ref, gt_live, gt_ref, tol_ms=(200, 300, 500, 1000)):
    """t_live: publish times (s); pos_ref: DISPLAYED ref position (s); gt_*: unit onsets in live/ref."""
    t_live, pos_ref = np.asarray(t_live), np.asarray(pos_ref)
    idx = np.clip(np.searchsorted(t_live, gt_live, side="right") - 1, 0, len(t_live) - 1)  # sample&hold
    err = pos_ref[idx] - np.asarray(gt_ref)
    run_max = np.maximum.accumulate(pos_ref)
    lat = np.array([t_live[k] - gl if (k := np.searchsorted(run_max, gr)) < len(t_live) else np.nan
                    for gl, gr in zip(gt_live, gt_ref)])                 # highlight latency (+ = late)
    return dict(pos_AAE_ms=1e3*np.mean(np.abs(err)), pos_bias_ms=1e3*np.mean(err),
                lat_median_ms=1e3*np.nanmedian(lat), lat_p90_ms=1e3*np.nanpercentile(lat, 90),
                lost_frac=float(np.mean(np.abs(err) > 2.0)),
                **{f"PCO@{t}": 100*np.mean(np.abs(err) <= t/1e3) for t in tol_ms})

pitfalls: License: the repo is private with no LICENSE file, and the .pt models are trained on LDC-licensed TIMIT. Do not copy code or checkpoints into a new or public project without written permission from the author (laurenceyoon / Jiyun Park). Reimplement from arXiv:2401.09200 (CC BY 4.0) and Dixon 2005. The resource audio (Sound of Music OST 'Edelweiss', what look like YouTube or rehearsal recordings of Lascia, the 꽃밭에서 performance) is probably copyrighted; keep it out of any public repository and use it only for private evaluation.

Don't trust the reference's OLTW numerics. It has the init length-matrix bugs, the '<=' edge-index bug, inconsistent exclusive/inclusive candidate coordinates (+40 ms bias), no BOTH step, and a multiplicative 0.98 diagonal that acts like time-varying forgetting. Reimplement with additive (1,1,2) weights and normalisation by i+j.

What the screen shows is not what the reference evaluates. The app publishes ref_pointer (window frontier) + ADJUST_DELAY 5 frames, while match_eval scores candi_history. Our harness must score the displayed position, causally, with real-time-paced streaming. The reference mock stream runs faster than real time and hides latency.

Start-up: the reference presets ref_pointer = w (5 s) and forces QUERY for 125 live frames, so the display shows ref ≈5.2 s during the first 5 s. There is no start detection, pause handling or re-localisation; a jump larger than the window (e.g. a skipped verse) is unrecoverable.

Live and ref feature mismatch: the reference live CRNN resets its LSTM state every 160 ms chunk and clamps dB per chunk (top_db=80 relative to the chunk maximum), while the ref is processed whole. Run the ref through the same chunked, stateful streaming path as the live input, or carry LSTM (h, c) across chunks.

Heavy work in the audio callback: the reference computes chroma and runs the CRNN inside the PyAudio callback, and feature_buffer is an unbounded queue, so latency can grow silently. Use a sounddevice callback that only enqueues, a worker thread, and a bounded queue that drops or reports overruns.

Chroma is key-dependent. winterreise_rt pitch-shifted SC06 to the HU33 key before evaluating, so the paper's numbers assume equal keys. Live singers may transpose (karaoke key change), so estimate the semitone offset (optimal transposition index on chroma) or use the minimum over circular chroma shifts.

Ground-truth caveats:
- *_score.csv 'start' is in a 120-bpm score timeline, NOT ref time. Map it through the warping path (score_frame, ref_frame) at 25 fps, after making the path strictly monotonic.
- For Ave Maria, score.wav was not rendered at 120 bpm; use offset × 1.5 s and verify.
- Pseudo ground truth inherits synctoolbox error (paper's offline AAE 302 ms; about 1/3 of notes off by more than 200 ms).
- The 꽃밭에서 score has a second sung part ('AI') that is not in the CSV.
- Ave Maria's score lyrics differ from lyrics.txt.

The LRC timestamps were hand-tapped with LRCgenerator.com: onsets only, unknown tap latency, and 'syllables' are tapped chunks ('E|very', 'for|ev|er'), not dictionary syllables. Evaluate mainly at word or line level, or re-annotate a subset in Sonic Visualiser for millisecond-level claims.

The reference's synctoolbox usage at 16 kHz is wrong for DLNCO: the pitch-onset filterbank is designed for 22050/4410/882 Hz. Load audio at 22050 Hz for synctoolbox, then convert the warping path to our 25 fps grid.

Version traps:
- librosa 1.0.0 (Aug 2026) removed get_duration(filename=) and expired other deprecations.
- synctoolbox 1.4.2 and libfmp 1.3.0 require librosa<1.0, so pin librosa 0.11.x if they are used. synctoolbox also pins numba<0.66 and numpy<2.5.
- pymatchmaker requires Python <3.13.
- requirements.txt's whisper==1.1.10 is the Graphite DB package.
- Replace attributedict with a dataclass.

Online evaluation with pandas Series subtraction or interp1d: if note counts differ between ref and target, pandas aligns by index and yields NaN. interp1d raises when onsets fall outside the path range (e.g. the tracker stopped early). Use explicit index-matched arrays and np.interp with clipping, and report coverage.

WebSocket design in the reference: every client runs its own 100 Hz loop that broadcasts to all clients (N² traffic), and stale-connection deletion by ascending index removes the wrong sockets. Use a single producer that pushes on change.

There is no Japanese ground truth anywhere in the reference resources, and no quantitative Korean evaluation (꽃밭에서 pseudo ground truth only). The Japanese and Korean evaluation sets must be built: annotate a few songs, or use synthetic warps of ref audio.
